plan: Comprehensive comparison guide for guard passing approaches: Headquarters Position vs Combat Base vs Knee Shield vs Pressure Passing vs Torreando. Include comparison table with: control type, risk level, energy cost, ideal scenarios, counter vulnerabilities. Add sections for: 'When to Use Each System', 'Beginner-Friendly Options', 'Competition vs Training Applications'. Target PAA questions: 'What is the best guard passing system?', 'Headquarters vs other passing styles?', 'How do I choose a passing system?'. Priority: HIGH - addresses comparison queries across multiple position articles.

Comprehensive safety guide for leg lock training and competition. Sections: 'Common Leg Lock Injuries' (heel hook catastrophic damage, ankle lock sprains, knee ligament tears), 'Tap Early Protocol' (why pain signals are delayed, damage before awareness), 'Safe Training Practices' (partner selection, progressive resistance, communication), 'Warning Signs of Injury', 'Rehabilitation Guidelines', 'Training Room Rules for Leg Locks'. Include safety checklist, injury severity matrix, and tap signal standardization. Target PAA: 'How dangerous are leg locks?', 'Are heel hooks safe?', 'When should I tap to leg locks?'. Priority: CRITICAL - safety content gap across all leg lock articles.

Definitive ruleset guide for leg lock legality across organizations and belt levels. Create comprehensive matrix table: IBJJF (white/blue/purple/brown/black), ADCC, EBI, NAGA, submission-only. Cover: straight ankle locks, heel hooks, knee bars, toe holds, calf slicers, reaping rules, 50-50 legality. Add sections: 'Understanding Reaping', 'What Changes at Each Belt', 'Competition-Specific Exceptions', 'No-Gi vs Gi Rules'. Include visual diagrams for legal/illegal leg positions. Target PAA: 'Is Ashi Garami legal in IBJJF?', 'When are heel hooks legal?', 'What belt can you do heel hooks?'. Priority: HIGH - competition planning essential.

Technical deep-dive on inside space control principle fundamental to leg entanglements and guard passing. Sections: 'What is Inside Space?' (definition, visual diagram), 'Why Inside Space Matters' (mechanical advantage, position advancement), 'How to Establish Inside Space' (step-by-step for various positions), 'Defending Against Inside Space Control', 'Inside Space in Different Contexts' (Ashi Garami, headquarters, guard passing, half guard). Include visual aids showing inside space concept, drills for developing awareness, common errors. Target PAA: 'What is inside space control?', 'How do you control inside space?', 'Why is inside space important in BJJ?'. Priority: HIGH - referenced across multiple articles but never fully explained.

Historical and technical overview of John Danaher's systematic passing methodology and its impact on modern BJJ. Sections: 'Origins of Systematic Passing', 'Headquarters Position as Central Hub', 'If-Then Decision Trees in Passing', 'Key Principles: Base, Posture, Pressure', 'Danaher's Influence on Competition Grappling', 'Evolution from Traditional Passing'. Include quotes from Danaher instruction, success of his students (Gordon Ryan, etc.), comparison to traditional passing. Target PAA: 'Who invented headquarters position?', 'What is systematic guard passing?', 'John Danaher passing system explained'. Priority: MEDIUM - adds credibility and historical context.

Detailed comparison of all Ashi Garami variations: Outside, Inside, Cross, Saddle, 50-50, Backside 50-50, Ushiro. Create comparison table: control quality, heel exposure, advancement pathways, submission options, legal/illegal status, difficulty level. Sections: 'Position Hierarchy Explained' (visual diagram), 'When to Use Each Variation', 'Transitional Pathways Between Variations', 'Strategic Considerations', 'Common Confusion Addressed'. Target PAA: 'What is the difference between Ashi Garami variations?', '50-50 vs Saddle?', 'Best Ashi Garami position for beginners?'. Priority: MEDIUM - clarifies terminology confusion.
